item.title: Balanced Forces on a Hanging Sign and a Sliding Puck
item.stimulus: A sign of mass 20 kg hangs at rest from two light cables. Cable 1 pulls on the sign up and to the left at 30° above the horizontal, with tension T₁. Cable 2 pulls on the sign up and to the right at 60° above the horizontal, with tension T₂. Use g = 10 m/s².

parts.prompt: Write the equations that express the condition for the sign to remain at rest, one for the horizontal direction and one for the vertical direction, in terms of T₁ and T₂.

criteria.text: Horizontal: T₁ cos 30° = T₂ cos 60°, from setting the net horizontal force equal to zero.
criteria.evidence: Response sets the sum of the horizontal force components equal to zero, giving T₁ cos 30° = T₂ cos 60° or an equivalent form.
criteria.fix: For an object at rest, write ΣFx = 0, resolving each tension with cosine of its angle from the horizontal.

criteria.text: Vertical: T₁ sin 30° + T₂ sin 60° = mg = 200 N, from setting the net vertical force equal to zero.
criteria.evidence: Response sets the sum of the vertical force components equal to zero, with the weight written as mg or 200 N.
criteria.fix: For an object at rest, write ΣFy = 0: the upward tension components together must equal the weight mg.

criteria.text: T₁ = 100 N, for example by solving the two equilibrium equations from part (a).
criteria.evidence: Response obtains T₁ = 100 N by any valid equilibrium calculation (solving the part (a) equations, a closed force triangle, or another valid method), or the value that follows correctly from its own part (a) equations.
criteria.fix: Solve the horizontal equation for T₂ in terms of T₁, substitute into the vertical equation, then check both equations with your values.

parts.prompt: Separately, a hockey puck slides due north at constant velocity across horizontal, frictionless ice. As it passes a player, the player's stick gives the puck a brief push directed due east. Describe what happens to the north component of the puck's velocity during the push. Justify your answer.

criteria.text: The north component stays constant because the forces in the north–south direction remain balanced (the push has no north–south component).
criteria.evidence: Response states the north velocity component is unchanged and links this to zero net force in the north–south direction.
criteria.fix: Analyze each direction separately: a velocity component changes only along a direction in which the forces are unbalanced.

parts.prompt: A passenger in a car that is braking places a water bottle on the car's flat, frictionless floor. The forces on the bottle (gravity and the normal force from the floor) are balanced, yet the passenger sees the bottle start to slide forward. Explain whether the braking car is an inertial reference frame.

criteria.text: The braking car is not an inertial frame: in that frame an object with zero net force changes its velocity, so Newton's first law is not verified there.
criteria.evidence: Response says the car is not an inertial frame because, in it, the bottle's velocity changes although the net force on the bottle is zero.
criteria.fix: Define an inertial frame as one where objects with zero net force keep a constant velocity, then test the observed motion against that.

item.model_answer:
(a) The sign is at rest, so the net force on it is zero in each direction. Take right and up as positive. The weight is mg = (20 kg)(10 m/s²) = 200 N.
Horizontal: T₂ cos 60° − T₁ cos 30° = 0, so T₁ cos 30° = T₂ cos 60°.
Vertical: T₁ sin 30° + T₂ sin 60° − 200 N = 0.

(b) From the horizontal equation, T₂ = T₁ cos 30°/cos 60° = √3 T₁ ≈ 1.732T₁.
Substituting into the vertical equation: 0.5T₁ + (1.732T₁)(0.866) = 200 N, so 0.5T₁ + 1.5T₁ = 2.0T₁ = 200 N.
T₁ = 100 N (and T₂ = 100√3 N ≈ 173 N).
Check: the horizontal components are (100 N)(0.866) = 86.6 N and (173.2 N)(0.5) = 86.6 N.

(c) The north component of the puck's velocity stays constant during the push, because no force acts on the puck in the north–south direction, so the forces in that direction stay balanced. (Gravity and the normal force from the ice balance vertically.) The push changes the velocity only in the east–west direction, where the force is unbalanced.

(d) The braking car is not an inertial reference frame. The net force on the bottle is zero, so by Newton's first law its velocity should stay constant; in the car's frame it was at rest and should stay at rest. Instead, the passenger sees it start moving forward. Newton's first law is not verified in the car's frame, so that frame is not inertial.
item.verification_python:
import math
m, g = 20.0, 10.0
W = m*g
assert W == 200.0
c30, c60 = math.cos(math.radians(30)), math.cos(math.radians(60))
s30, s60 = math.sin(math.radians(30)), math.sin(math.radians(60))
ratio = c30/c60
assert abs(ratio - math.sqrt(3)) < 1e-12
assert abs(ratio - 1.732) < 0.001
T1 = W/(s30 + ratio*s60)
T2 = ratio*T1
assert abs(s30 + ratio*s60 - 2.0) < 1e-12
assert abs(ratio*s60 - 1.5) < 1e-12
assert abs(T1 - 100) < 1e-9
assert abs(T2 - 100*math.sqrt(3)) < 1e-9
assert abs(T2 - 173) < 0.5
assert abs(T1*c30 - T2*c60) < 1e-9
assert abs(T1*c30 - 86.6) < 0.01
assert abs(173.2*0.5 - 86.6) < 1e-9
assert abs(T2 - 173.2) < 0.01
assert abs(T1*s30 + T2*s60 - W) < 1e-9
assert abs(s60 - 0.866) < 0.001
# force triangle: angle between cables is 90 degrees, so T1 = W sin 30 deg
assert abs(W*math.sin(math.radians(30)) - T1) < 1e-9
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')
